title: Abdominal examination: right iliac fossa mass

related.why: The stoma that may follow a right hemicolectomy

brief.scenario: Mrs Margaret Dunn, 72, has been referred with four months of tiredness and weight loss. Her GP's blood tests show iron-deficiency anaemia (haemoglobin 94 g/L).
brief.task: Examine her abdomen. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Hands, eyes, neck, then look, feel, percuss, listen; describe the mass; offer the rest.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Finding the mass and forgetting Virchow's node, the liver and the rectal examination.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Could you lie flat with one pillow? I'll start with your hands."

grid.label: Preparation
grid.fail: Starts palpating without consent or asking about pain.
grid.pass: Introduces, gains consent, lies her flat, exposes the abdomen while keeping her covered elsewhere, and asks about pain.
grid.high: Offers a chaperone, kneels to the bed's level, and watches her face while palpating.

grid.label: Hands, eyes and nodes
grid.pass: Hands (clubbing, pallor, koilonychia), conjunctivae, sclerae, and the left supraclavicular fossa for Virchow's node.
grid.high: Links findings to the story: pallor and koilonychia fit iron deficiency; a Virchow's node or jaundice suggests spread.

grid.label: Inspection and palpation
grid.fail: Palpates deeply first, or misses the mass.
grid.pass: Inspects for distension, scars and visible masses; light then deep palpation of all nine regions; liver, spleen and kidneys.
grid.high: Feels for an enlarged, irregular liver as a sign of metastases, and ballots the right kidney to separate it from the mass.

grid.label: Describing the mass
grid.fail: Says 'there's a mass' with no description.
grid.pass: Site, size, shape, surface, edge, consistency, tenderness, mobility, movement with breathing, percussion note and pulsatility.
grid.high: Uses the findings to place it: not ballotable, doesn't move with breathing, can get above it, so bowel rather than kidney or liver.

grid.label: Percussion, auscultation and completion
grid.fail: Finishes without offering a rectal examination or hernial orifices.
grid.pass: Percusses the mass and for shifting dullness; listens for bowel sounds; offers hernial orifices, external genitalia and a rectal examination with a chaperone.
grid.high: Explains shifting dullness looks for ascites from peritoneal spread, and the rectal examination looks for blood or a rectal mass.

grid.label: Presentation and differential
grid.fail: Offers appendicitis first in a well, anaemic 72-year-old.
grid.pass: Presents a firm, irregular right iliac fossa mass with pallor; caecal cancer first, then appendix mass, Crohn's disease and ovarian mass.
grid.high: Orders the differential by age and story, and names the key negatives: no liver edge, no ascites, no Virchow's node.

grid.label: Suspected cancer pathway
grid.fail: Asks the GP to send a FIT first, or books a routine clinic.
grid.borderline: Knows the tests are urgent but tells the GP to re-refer her on a cancer pathway.
grid.pass: States she meets the NG12 criteria and stays on the suspected cancer pathway (28 days); arranges her tests from clinic.
grid.high: Adds that NICE says 'offer' FIT for a mass or iron-deficiency anaemia, but referral shouldn't wait for it with a palpable mass.

grid.label: Investigations
grid.pass: Arranges colonoscopy (or CT colonography if unfit) and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis to stage.
grid.high: Adds gastroscopy for iron-deficiency anaemia, and images the whole colon for a second cancer before surgery.

high.speaker: candidate

Given her age, weight loss and anaemia, this is caecal cancer until proven otherwise; less likely an appendix mass, Crohn's disease or an ovarian mass.

high.speaker: candidate

failures.move: Skipping the hands, eyes and neck.
failures.consequence: Misses the pallor that supports iron deficiency and a Virchow's node that suggests spread.
Can't tell bowel from kidney, liver or ovary, so the differential is wrong.
A rectal mass or blood is missed.

failures.move: Sending her back to the GP for a FIT first.
failures.consequence: Delays a cancer diagnosis; NICE says referral shouldn't wait for FIT when there's a palpable mass.

recovery.line: Before I finish, I'd like to feel above the left collarbone for an enlarged node.

recovery.when: You're not sure the mass is separate from the kidney
recovery.line: I'd like to ballot the kidney, to see whether the mass moves with it.

knowledge.fact: NICE: offer FIT to adults with an abdominal mass or iron-deficiency anaemia; refer if FIT is at least 10 µg Hb/g. With a mass, don't delay referral for FIT.
Suspected cancer pathway: diagnosis or ruling out within 28 days.
Iron-deficiency anaemia in men and postmenopausal women: gastroscopy and colonoscopy; CT colonography if unsuitable.
Suspected colon cancer: colonoscopy or CT colonography; stage with CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis.
Appendix mass treated without surgery at 40 or over: colonoscopy and interval CT.

recall.trap: A FIT isn't needed before referral when there's a palpable mass.
recall.finish: Colonoscopy, gastroscopy and staging CT on the suspected cancer pathway.

sources.supports: Offer quantitative FIT to guide referral in adults with an abdominal mass, a change in bowel habit or iron-deficiency anaemia, or aged 60 and over with anaemia even without iron deficiency (1.3.1); suspected cancer pathway referral if FIT at least 10 micrograms Hb per gram of faeces (1.3.2); if FIT below 10 or not returned, referral should not be delayed if there is strong clinical concern, for example an abdominal mass (1.3.3); suspected cancer pathway referral: diagnosis or ruling out of cancer within 28 days (glossary)

partner.opening: Please examine this patient's abdomen. A chaperone is available. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mrs Margaret Dunn, 72, a retired teacher. You've felt tired for four months and lost about 6 kg without trying. Your bowels are a bit looser than usual. No pain. You're worried it's something serious but haven't said so to anyone. Accept a chaperone if offered.

reveals.finding: Pale palmar creases; koilonychia. No clubbing.
Pale conjunctivae. No jaundice. No left supraclavicular node.
No distension or scars. Mass in the right iliac fossa. Liver and spleen not palpable. Right kidney ballotable and separate from the mass.
6 × 5 cm, firm, irregular, non-tender; can get above it; slightly mobile side to side; doesn't move with respiration; dull to percussion; not pulsatile.

reveals.trigger: Percusses for shifting dullness and auscultates
reveals.finding: No shifting dullness. Normal bowel sounds.

reveals.trigger: Offers a rectal examination, hernial orifices and genitalia
reveals.finding: Say: "Thank you; assume these are normal, with brown stool and no blood on the glove."
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: What is your differential for a right iliac fossa mass?
push.expect: Caecal cancer; appendix mass or abscess; Crohn's disease; ovarian mass; others such as lymphoma or a transplanted kidney.

push.question: How do you know it isn't the kidney?
push.expect: Can get above it, not ballotable, kidney felt separately.

push.question: Does she need a FIT first?
push.expect: No: she meets NG12 criteria and stays on the suspected cancer pathway; with a palpable mass referral isn't delayed for FIT.

curveballs.prompt: Instead, a 55-year-old man has five days of right iliac fossa pain, fever and a tender mass. CT shows an appendix abscess.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Antibiotics with percutaneous drainage if available, or laparoscopic surgery where the expertise exists; at 40 or over, colonoscopy and interval CT to exclude a tumour.

curveballs.prompt: Her FIT result comes back at 4 µg Hb/g.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Doesn't change the plan: with a palpable mass, referral and investigation aren't delayed.

curveballs.prompt: She can't tolerate bowel preparation for colonoscopy.
curveballs.safeAnswer: CT colonography is an acceptable alternative.
